chunks: Forbidden to you are carrion and blood, and the flesh of the swine, and that which has been consecrated in the name of any other than God. If one is obliged by necessity to eat it without intending to transgress, or reverting to it, he is not guilty of sin; for God is forgiving and kind.

key_terms.الْمَيْتَة: Carrion (meat of an animal that died naturally without being slaughtered)
key_terms.فَلَا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ: Then there is no sin upon him
key_terms.مَا أُهِلَ بِهِ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ: That which was consecrated/sacrificed in the name of other than God

ai.seo_question: What are the four main forbidden foods in Islam and when is it permissible to eat them out of necessity?
ai.summary: This foundational verse from Surah Al-Baqarah delineates the four primary categories of prohibited foods (khaba'ith) while establishing the legal principle of 'durar' (necessity), which permits their consumption during genuine need. Shia jurists emphasize that the exemption applies only when one is not a 'bagh' (exceeding limits) or 'ad' (habitual), ensuring that necessity does not become a license for gluttony or regular practice.
